title: How to Grill Halloumi Cheese Without Sticking on a BBQ Mat
meta_description: Stop losing your cheese to the grates! Learn how to grill halloumi on grill mat surfaces for perfectly charred, non-stick results every single time.
html:
Halloumi is the ultimate grilling cheese because of its high melting point. While other cheeses turn into a gooey puddle the moment they hit the heat, halloumi holds its shape, offering a salty, savory bite with a satisfying sear. However, if you've ever tried grilling it directly on open grates, you know the struggle: one wrong move and half your slice is stuck to the metal.

The secret to a stress-free experience is learning how to grill halloumi on grill mat surfaces. By using a barrier, you get those beautiful golden-brown marks without the anxiety of the cheese fusing to your BBQ. Here is exactly how to do it using BBQ Grill Mats for a perfect result.

Why Use a Grill Mat for Halloumi?

When you place cheese directly on a hot grill, the proteins and sugars caramelize and bond to the metal. This is why halloumi often sticks or tears when you try to flip it. A non-stick surface breaks that bond.

Using BBQ Grill Mats allows you to grill delicate foods without flare-ups or sticking. Because the mat distributes heat evenly across the surface, you avoid those aggressive hot spots that can burn the outside of the cheese before the inside warms through. Plus, it keeps your grill cleaner, as the melted fats stay on the mat rather than dripping into the coals and causing smoke spikes.

Preparing Your Halloumi for the Grill

Preparation is key to ensuring the cheese doesn't slide around or stick. Start by slicing your halloumi into thick slabs—about 1/2 inch to 3/4 inch is ideal. If the slices are too thin, they can overcook and become rubbery too quickly.

Pat the slices dry with a paper towel. Surface moisture creates steam, which can prevent that crisp, brown crust from forming. While halloumi is naturally salty, you can lightly brush both sides with a high-smoke-point oil, like avocado or grapeseed oil. Even though you are using a non-stick mat, a tiny bit of oil helps conduct the heat and enhances the sear.

Step-by-Step: How to Grill Halloumi on Grill Mat Surfaces

Follow these steps to get the perfect char without the cleanup headache:

  • Preheat Your Grill: Get your BBQ to medium-high heat. If you're using gas, aim for around 400°F.
  • Position the Mat: Place your BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grates and let them heat up for 2-3 minutes.
  • Place the Cheese: Carefully lay your halloumi slices onto the hot mat. You should hear a gentle sizzle immediately.
  • Leave it Alone: This is the hardest part. Resist the urge to move the cheese for 2-4 minutes. The cheese needs time to develop a crust; if you move it too soon, you lose the sear.
  • The Flip: Once the bottom is golden brown, use a thin spatula to lift and flip the slice.
  • Finish: Grill for another 2-3 minutes on the second side until evenly charred.

Flavor Pairings and Serving Suggestions

Grilled halloumi is a powerhouse of flavor, but it benefits from a bit of acidity to balance the saltiness. Once you remove the cheese from the mat, try these simple additions:

A drizzle of honey and a sprinkle of chili flakes create a sweet-and-spicy contrast that is a crowd favorite. For a Mediterranean vibe, squeeze fresh lemon juice over the hot slices and garnish with fresh mint or oregano. If you're serving it as part of a meal, it works brilliantly inside a toasted pita with cucumber, tomato, and a dollop of tzatziki.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Grill Mats

One of the best parts about using BBQ Grill Mats is that they are reusable. After your grilling session, let the mat cool down before handling. For light residue, a simple wipe with a damp cloth and mild dish soap usually does the trick.

For tougher bits of burnt cheese, soak the mat in warm, soapy water for ten minutes. Avoid using metal scrubbers or steel wool, as these can scratch the non-stick coating. A soft sponge or a nylon brush will keep your mats in top shape for your next BBQ session.

FAQ

Can I use a grill mat on a charcoal grill?

Yes, you can use these mats on charcoal grills. Just ensure the mat is centered and the heat is evenly distributed. The mat helps prevent the cheese from falling through the wider gaps often found in charcoal grates.

Does using a mat prevent the grill marks?

You will still get a beautiful, golden-brown sear. While you may not get the deep, charred "lines" of a direct grate, the overall browning is more uniform, and the taste is identical.

How thick should I slice the halloumi?

Aim for 1/2 to 3/4 of an inch. Slices that are too thin will cook through too fast and may shrink or toughen, while slices that are too thick might not heat through to the center before the outside burns.
